fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeNiMo alloy, boron microalloying, mechanical alloying, and coarse-grained same-alloy control do not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi2.1-versus-DS2205 thermal-shock comparison.

The test environment is changed from deionized water over 25–100 °C to 3.5 wt.% NaCl without reproducing the specified load, frequency, stroke, counter-body, thermal cycles, or repassivation protocol.
The experiment jointly changes processing, grain size, boron content, precipitates, and passive-film behavior, so it cannot identify which proposed mediator causes any improvement.

Wear rate, friction, and separate polarization measurements do not decompose simultaneous tribocorrosion into mechanical wear, corrosion, and interaction terms; the claim that combined loss will be less than their sum is therefore neither directly tested nor adequately supported.

The cited evidence supports general benefits of Mo, selected coatings, oxidation layers, or boron modification, but does not establish the specific causal chain from nanocrystalline grain refinement to a hard, low-friction passive film in the proposed bulk alloy.
explanation: The response addresses the general tribocorrosion problem and shares part of the target mechanism: resistance depends on whether a protective interfacial film can form, remain mechanically stable, and reform after sliding. Its boundaries and falsification rule are also broadly sensible. However, it is a different materials hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the target study. It omits the eutectic L12/B2 lamellar HEA, DS2205 comparator, rapid 1100 °C thermal shocks, deionized-water temperature series, and the nonmonotonic minimum in degradation near 50 °C. It also misses the target's temperature-dependent transition among abrasion, polishing, and oxide/third-body wear. The evidence makes the alternative plausible at a general level, but it does not validate the asserted nanocrystalline passive-film mechanism or negative wear–corrosion synergy. A discriminating test would require factorial controls for processing and boron, in situ electrochemical current during sliding, mechanically protected or cathodically protected wear controls, corrosion-only controls, and direct passive-film chemistry and thickness measurements.
